sections.body:
| Concept | Remember |
|--------|--------|
| Generic function | `function f<T>(value: T): T` |
| Generic interface | `interface Repository<T>` |
| Generic class | `class Storage<T>` |
| Generic constraint | `T extends SomeType` |
| Multiple parameters | `<T, U>` |
| Default parameter type | `<T = unknown>` |
| keyof | Extract property keys |
| typeof | Query a value's static type |
| Indexed access | `T[K]` |
| Partial | All properties optional |
| Required | Remove optional modifiers |
| Readonly | Add readonly modifiers |
| Pick | Select properties |
| Omit | Exclude properties |
| Record | Key-value mapping |
| ReturnType | Extract function return type |
| Parameters | Extract argument tuple |
| Awaited | Unwrap awaited type |
| Exclude | Remove union members |
| Extract | Retain union members |
| NonNullable | Remove null and undefined |
| Conditional type | `T extends U ? X : Y` |
| Mapped type | `[K in keyof T]: T[K]` |
| infer | Capture a matched type |
| Branded type | Primitive or object type plus distinguishing marker |
| NoInfer | Block inference from a selected type position |
| Distribution | Conditional evaluated for union members |
| Tool registry | Type map + generic indexed access |
| Runtime validation | Zod or equivalent schema validator |

## What should you prioritize for your interview?

These are recommended study priorities for your job description, not statistical interview probabilities.

quiz.question: What is a branded type?
options: Captures a type inside a conditional pattern.
Evaluates a conditional separately for union members in qualifying cases.
A value satisfying all member types.
A technique that adds a static distinguishing marker to an existing structural type.
quiz.explanation: A technique that adds a static distinguishing marker to an existing structural type.

quiz.question: Why use branded types for identifiers?
options: To represent impossible values and detect unhandled cases.
Interviewer: Your supervisor dynamically selects an agent name, but sometimes the requested agent does not exist.
To prevent semantically different IDs with the same primitive representation from being accidentally interchanged.
quiz.explanation: To prevent semantically different IDs with the same primitive representation from being accidentally interchanged.

quiz.question: Do brands exist at runtime?
options: Interviewer: Every agent must implement browser automation, retrieval, email sending and code generation, even when those capabilities are unnecessary.
They may become never or make the resulting type impossible.
Interviewer: Your LLM generates the correct tool name but incorrect argument properties.
Not in this phantom-brand implementation. The runtime values remain ordinary strings or numbers.
quiz.explanation: Not in this phantom-brand implementation. The runtime values remain ordinary strings or numbers.

quiz.question: Are branded types security guarantees?
options: Interviewer: Your RAG service imports the provider service, and the provider service imports the RAG service.
Ordinary enums generally have runtime representations; literal unions are erased.
Interviewer: Another developer changes the return value of an asynchronous LLM service.
No. They improve compile-time correctness but do not replace validation, authentication or authorization.
quiz.explanation: No. They improve compile-time correctness but do not replace validation, authentication or authorization. This is the most important practical implementation in this module.
